desc:
The array nums contains distinct integers. Every entry of queries is some value that occurs in nums.

For a query value v located at index p in nums, its next greater value is the first number to the right of position p that is larger than v. Return an array with one entry per query: its next greater value, or -1 if no larger number exists to its right.

Example: nums = [4, 1, 2, 7, 3, 5], queries = [1, 4, 3, 5] gives [2, 7, 5, -1].
constraints: -10<sup>9</sup> ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10<sup>9</sup> and all values in nums are distinct
Every query value occurs in nums (a query may repeat)
hints: For one query you can find its position and scan right. Doing that for every query is slow when there are many queries. Can you answer for all numbers of nums in one pass?
A number that has not yet met a larger number to its right is still 'waiting'. When a larger number arrives it answers every waiting number smaller than it.

Scan nums from left to right with a stack of waiting values. While the top is smaller than the current value, pop it and store the current value as its answer in a dictionary. Then answer queries by dictionary lookup (default -1).
editorial: Compute the next greater value of every element of nums once, then look the queries up. Use a stack of values that are still waiting for a greater number. The stack is non-increasing from bottom to top: when the current number x arrives, all waiting numbers smaller than x find their answer in x, because x is the first number to their right that beats them. Pop them and record x as their answer.

Then push x. Values left on the stack at the end have no greater number to their right and keep the default -1. Because the values are distinct a dictionary keyed by value is safe. Total time is O(n + q) and extra space is O(n).
